samples.summary: Collapsed blame labels disappear entirely once the run's first line scrolls out of the viewport
samples.evidence: `computeBlameLabels` collapses consecutive same-author lines so that only the FIRST line of a run carries the name (`labels.push(author !== null && author !== previous ? author : '')`, line 78), and `lineMarker` returns `null` for a blank label (line 217). CodeMirror gutters only render markers for lines in the current viewport (`view.viewportLineBlocks`), so when the first line of a run is above the visible viewport — the common case in a note where one author wrote a long stretch — every visible line renders an empty gutter element and the user sees no author at all. The collapse is computed over the whole document instead of per rendered viewport, so the feature silently shows nothing exactly where it is most needed (scrolled into a long note). The design doc (docs/design/notes/notes.md:515) records the collapse intent but never addresses viewport rendering.

samples.summary: Label recomputation is O(lines × runs) on every keystroke, and run count grows one per edit
samples.evidence: `authorOfRange` restarts its scan at span index 0 for every line (`for (const span of spans) { if (span.to <= from) continue; ... }`, lines 44-50) — it only breaks past the line's end, never skips the prefix — and `computeBlameLabels` calls it once per document line (line 71). The tracker re-runs the whole walk plus `store.getAuthorSpans()` (a full CRDT node walk) on every `docChanged` update (lines 145-153), i.e. per keystroke. Because `YorkieNoteStore.editText` stamps a distinct `t: Date.now()` on every insert (yorkie-note-store.ts:192), adjacent runs by the same author never merge, so the run count grows roughly one per edit for the life of the note. A 500-line note with a few thousand runs is ~10^6 span comparisons per keystroke, plus an extra dispatched transaction — perceptible typing lag that worsens monotonically with the note's edit history.

samples.summary: Gutter paints stale/shifted labels between the doc change and the microtask repaint
samples.evidence: The gutter re-renders on any `docChanged` update (CodeMirror re-renders viewport gutter elements regardless of `lineMarkerChange`), but the fresh labels are only published to the DOM by the empty transaction queued in `scheduleRepaint` (queueMicrotask, line 176). So after every edit that inserts/removes lines, the gutter is painted once with labels indexed for the previous line numbering — labels appear on the wrong lines for one frame. The same window is wider for remote changes: `note-sync.ts:41-51` applies a multi-edit remote change as one transaction per edit, while `getAuthorSpans()` already reflects ALL of the CRDT's ops, so the intermediate transactions compute labels from spans whose offsets do not match `update.state.doc` at all.

samples.summary: getAuthorSpans guards only for a missing content, not for the mis-built content object ensureText exists to repair
samples.evidence: `getAuthorSpans()` does `if (!content) return []` and then calls `content.values()` (lines 201-208). `notes-view.tsx:57-73` (`ensureText`) documents that documents persisted by an earlier build can carry `root.content` as a plain `{ context, text }` object with no CRDT methods, and only repairs it on writable mounts. On such a document `content.values` is not a function, so the tracker's constructor (`blame-gutter.ts:138`) would throw during editor initialization rather than degrade to no labels. Reachable only if the gutter is enabled on a mount where `ensureText` was skipped (read-only), which today never passes `showAuthors`, hence low confidence — but the guard is narrower than the failure mode the neighbouring code says exists.

samples.summary: Length cap can split a surrogate pair, re-introducing the lone surrogate the strip removed
samples.evidence: `sanitizeDisplayName` strips `\p{Cs}` (lone surrogates) first and only then does `.slice(0, MAX_DISPLAY_NAME_LENGTH)` (lines 51-55). Slicing at a fixed UTF-16 offset can cut through a valid surrogate pair (e.g. a name of emoji), leaving a lone high surrogate as the last code unit — exactly the class of code point the `\p{Cs}` strip was there to remove, now rendered as U+FFFD. The cap is also applied before `.trim()`, so a name with leading spaces is capped shorter than 64 visible characters.

samples.summary: An extra empty transaction per edit may disturb IME composition
samples.evidence: `scheduleRepaint` dispatches `view.dispatch({ annotations: [blameRepaint.of(true)] })` in a microtask after every edit whose labels changed (line 179) — i.e. on essentially every keystroke while the gutter is on. Dispatching transactions into CodeMirror while an IME composition is active is a known way to abort the composition (CM syncs the DOM on update and drops the composition decoration); with Korean/Japanese input the in-progress syllable can be committed or lost. Not reproduced here, hence low confidence, but the repaint is unconditional with respect to `view.composing`.

samples.summary: MemNoteStore batch records no undo unit when only authorship changed, losing the prior authorship
samples.evidence: `batch()` records an undo entry only `if (this.batchBefore.text !== this.text)` (line 149). Now that `MemState` also carries `authors`, a batch that replaces text with identical text (select a word, retype it, or a formatting toggle that round-trips) rewrites `this.authors` but pushes no undo unit, so the previous authorship is unrecoverable and undo skips straight past the edit. The condition compares only the text half of the state it is snapshotting.

samples.summary: MemNoteStore.splice spreads an array of insert.length arguments into splice
samples.evidence: `this.authors.splice(from, to - from, ...new Array<MemAuthorMark>(insert.length).fill(mark))` (lines 131-135) passes one argument per inserted character. A large paste (roughly >64k–125k characters, engine dependent) throws `RangeError: too many function arguments`, turning an edit that previously succeeded into a crash. The store is described as test/dev only, which bounds the impact, but the failure is new with this change.

samples.summary: Tracker never recomputes labels when authorship changes without a document change
samples.evidence: `update()` returns immediately unless `update.docChanged` (line 146). Authorship can change without the text changing: a Yorkie snapshot that re-materializes `root.content` with the same string but different run attributes, or an attribute-only remote change (a peer re-styling a run it did not write is explicitly called out as possible in yorkie-note-store.ts:27-29). In those cases the gutter keeps showing the previous labels indefinitely, since nothing else recomputes or schedules a repaint.

samples.summary: Share-link note mounts can never show the gutter, though authorship is recorded into the note they read
samples.evidence: `<NotesView readOnly={readOnly} viewMode={readOnly ? "view" : "both"} />` passes no `showAuthors`, so it defaults to `false` (notes-view.tsx:88) and there is no toolbar on that route to toggle it. A share-link editor therefore also never records authorship, while the same document accumulates names from notes-detail users — the feature is silently unavailable on one of the two mounts of NotesView.

verdict.reason: The code is as quoted — computeBlameLabels collapses runs document-wide (blame-gutter.ts:78) and lineMarker returns null for a blank label (blame-gutter.ts:217), so a viewport wholly inside one author's run renders only empty gutter cells. But this is the explicitly specified behavior, not a logic error: docs/design/notes/notes.md:514-515 states "Consecutive lines by one author collapse to a single label," and blame-gutter.test.ts:37-45 pins that contract. Every rendered label is correct for its line; the index math (doc.lineAt(line.from).number - 1 against an array built over lines 1..doc.lines) has no off-by-one, a missing labels entry degrades to null rather than crashing, and there is no state, ordering, async, or data-loss problem. The complaint is that the accepted collapse rule yields fewer visible labels when scrolled — a UX/design tradeoff for an optional reading aid that is off by default (editor.ts:271, 356) and documented as "a reading aid, not an audit trail" (notes.md:557). Switching to a viewport-relative collapse is a design change, not a correctness fix, so it falls outside this lens's rubric (wrong conditions, boundary errors, inverted logic, missing-guard crashes, races, swallowed errors, broken invariants) and does not gate merge.

verdict.reason: The described code exists exactly as quoted (authorOfRange restarts at span 0 per line, blame-gutter.ts:44-50; called per line at 71-80; recomputed with a fresh getAuthorSpans() on every docChanged at 145-153; Date.now() stamped per insert at yorkie-note-store.ts:192 with no run merging in getAuthorSpans, 200-228). However the finding alleges only an algorithmic cost/latency problem (O(lines x runs) per keystroke, growing with edit history) — not a wrong result, boundary error, inverted condition, null crash, data loss, or async/ordering mistake. The labels computed are correct: the `break` is sound because getAuthorSpans emits spans in ascending document order, so the prefix scan is redundant rather than wrong. The extra dispatched transaction cannot loop or race: it carries only an annotation (line 179) so update() returns at line 146 (`if (!update.docChanged) return`), it is coalesced by repaintQueued (173-181), guarded by `destroyed` (178, set at 156-159), and skipped when labels are unchanged (151). No leak: labelsByView is a WeakMap cleared in destroy() (98,158); growing span count is inherent to Yorkie's per-node CRDT text model, not state this code accumulates. The feature is additionally opt-in and off by default (editor.ts:189, 356, 388), and the cited ~10^6 integer comparisons are single-digit milliseconds, not a crash or broken core flow. Performance/scalability belongs to another lens, so this is out of scope for the correctness rubric.
